question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the finite region bounded between the curves $y={x}^{3}$ and $y=\sqrt[3]{x},$ in the first quadrant?

- It is a type I region
- It is a type II region
- It's neither a type I nor a type II region
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}y={x}^{3}\, & ⟹\,x=\sqrt[3]{y} \\ y=\sqrt[3]{x}\, & ⟹\,x={y}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114484/assets/899357795c6d5b81d3cb619d71493ad787645697fe1f2fcecda78c1b875f388e.png)

We have the following:

- Any vertical line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{3}\le y\le \sqrt[3]{x}}.
$$

So, this is a type I region.

- Any horizontal line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,{y}^{3}\le x\le \sqrt[3]{y}}.
$$

So, this is a type II region.

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.
